questions.prompt: Walk me through what happens between a setState call and the pixels changing on screen.
questions.zh: 从调用 setState 到屏幕上的像素发生变化，中间都发生了什么？给我讲一遍。
outline: setState schedules an update; React batches updates from the same event
Render phase: call components, diff the new tree against the old
Commit phase: apply DOM changes, then run layout effects and effects
Rendering can be interrupted in concurrent mode; commit is always synchronous
Finally the browser does layout and paint

chunks.zh: 协调（对比新旧树、算出最小变更）

followUps: Why must components be pure during the render phase?
What does a transition change about this flow?

questions.prompt: How does Vue 3's reactivity system track dependencies, and why did it move away from the Vue 2 approach?
questions.zh: Vue 3 的响应式系统是怎么追踪依赖的？为什么放弃了 Vue 2 的做法？
outline: Vue 3 wraps objects in Proxies; Vue 2 used Object.defineProperty getters and setters
Reading a property inside an effect tracks it; writing triggers dependent effects
Proxies also catch added or deleted properties and array index changes
Caveat: destructuring a reactive object loses reactivity; use refs or toRefs
Computed values are cached and only recalculated when dependencies change
followUps: When would you use ref versus reactive?
How does Vue batch DOM updates after several state changes?

questions.prompt: React re-renders a whole subtree by default, while Vue tracks which components depend on which state. How does that change the way you optimize each?
questions.zh: React 默认重新渲染整棵子树，而 Vue 会追踪哪个组件依赖哪份状态。这个差别怎样影响你对两者的优化思路？
outline: React: a state change re-runs the component and all its children
So you memoize, keep props referentially stable, and move state down
Vue: only components that read the changed state re-render
Vue's pitfalls differ: huge reactive objects, deep watchers, lost reactivity
Compilers narrow the gap: React Compiler, Vue's static hoisting and patch flags
followUps: Which model do you find easier to reason about in a large codebase, and why?

questions.prompt: How do you decide what state goes in a global store, what stays local, and what belongs in a server-cache library?
questions.zh: 哪些状态放全局 store、哪些留在组件本地、哪些交给服务端缓存库，你是怎么决定的？
outline: Default to local state; lift it only when siblings need it
Treat API data as server state: caching and refetching belong to a query library
Global store only for truly shared client state: session, theme, cross-page flows
The URL is state too: filters, pagination, selected tab
Do not store what you can derive
followUps: What bugs have you seen from copying server data into a client store?

questions.prompt: When does React Context stop being enough, and what do you reach for instead?
questions.zh: React Context 在什么情况下就不够用了？这时候你会换成什么？
outline: Context is dependency injection, not a state manager; fine for rarely changing values
Every consumer re-renders when the provider value changes; there are no selectors
Mitigate by splitting contexts or memoizing the provider value
For frequent updates use a store with selectors: Zustand, Redux Toolkit, Jotai
Weigh the extra dependency against the size of the app

chunks.term: subscribe to a slice of the state

chunks.zh: 根据 action 算出下一个状态的纯函数

followUps: How would you migrate a large app off an overgrown Redux store?

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time you tracked down and fixed a serious front-end performance problem.
questions.zh: 讲一次你排查并解决严重前端性能问题的经历。
outline: Situation: which metric was bad and how users were affected
Measure before fixing: field data, profiler, flame chart, not guesswork
Name the root cause: long task, oversized bundle, re-render storm
Action: the fix you chose and the trade-off it carried
Result: before-and-after numbers, plus a guard against regression
followUps: How did you make sure it didn't regress later?
What would you have done if that fix hadn't been enough?

questions.prompt: Our INP is poor on a page with heavy interactions. How would you approach improving it?
questions.zh: 我们有个交互很重的页面，INP 指标很差。你会怎么着手改善？
outline: Use field data to find the slow interactions, then reproduce them in the profiler
Break the delay down: input delay, processing time, presentation delay
Split long tasks, yield to the main thread, mark non-urgent updates as transitions
Move heavy computation to a web worker; virtualize long lists
Shrink the DOM and avoid layout thrashing inside handlers
followUps: Why can lab data and field data disagree on this metric?

questions.prompt: Your JavaScript bundle has doubled over the past year. How do you find out why and bring it back down?
questions.zh: 过去一年你们的 JavaScript 包体积翻了一倍。你怎么查原因，又怎么把它降回去？
outline: Run a bundle analyzer; look for duplicated and oversized dependencies
Split by route and lazy-load rarely used features
Check tree shaking: ESM builds, side-effect flags, barrel files
Replace heavy libraries; stop shipping polyfills that modern browsers do not need
Add a size budget in CI so it cannot creep back

chunks.zh: 给旧浏览器补上缺失 API 的代码

followUps: How do you decide where to put the split points?

questions.prompt: When would you choose server-side rendering over a client-rendered SPA, and what does it cost you?
questions.zh: 什么情况下你会选服务端渲染而不是纯客户端渲染的单页应用？代价是什么？
outline: SSR helps first paint and SEO on public, content-heavy pages
Costs: server load, hydration work, more complex caching and deployment
The page can look ready before it is actually interactive
Alternatives: static generation for stable content, streaming for slow data
An internal dashboard behind a login rarely needs it
followUps: How would you cache server-rendered pages that contain personalized content?

questions.prompt: What causes hydration mismatches, and how have you debugged and prevented them?
questions.zh: 水合不匹配是什么原因造成的？你是怎么排查和预防的？
outline: Server and client produce different output from the same component
Usual suspects: dates, time zones, random IDs, window checks, browser extensions
Invalid HTML nesting too, because the browser rewrites the DOM
Fix: render client-only values after mount, or pass them down from the server
React recovers by re-rendering on the client up to the nearest Suspense boundary

chunks.term: render it on the client only

followUps: Why is suppressing the warning usually the wrong fix?

questions.prompt: How do React Server Components change the way you structure an app, compared with classic SSR?
questions.zh: 和传统的服务端渲染相比，React 服务端组件怎样改变了你组织应用的方式？
outline: Server Components run only on the server and add nothing to the bundle
Classic SSR still ships and hydrates every component; Server Components are never hydrated
Fetch data inside the component, next to where it is used
Push the client boundary down to the interactive leaves
Constraints: no state or effects, and props crossing the boundary must serialize
followUps: What kinds of apps don't benefit much from Server Components?
How do you handle mutations in that model?

questions.prompt: Why did Vue introduce the Composition API, and how do composables compare with React hooks?
questions.zh: Vue 为什么要引入组合式 API？组合式函数和 React 的 hooks 相比怎么样？
outline: The Options API scatters one feature across data, methods, and watchers
The Composition API groups logic by feature and extracts it into composables
It replaces mixins: no name clashes, and each value has a clear source
setup runs once per instance; React hooks re-run on every render
So no dependency arrays or stale closures, but refs need .value

chunks.zh: 闭包陷阱（拿到的是旧值）

followUps: Would you still use the Options API for anything today?

questions.prompt: A Vue page that holds a large data set feels sluggish. Where do you look?
questions.zh: 一个持有大量数据的 Vue 页面用起来很卡。你会从哪里查起？
outline: Profile first: Vue devtools timeline and the browser performance panel
Deep reactivity on big objects is costly; use shallowRef or markRaw
Virtualize long lists and give v-for stable keys
Use computed for derived values; avoid deep watchers on large trees
Keep props stable so child components can skip updates
followUps: Why is using the array index as a key a problem?

questions.prompt: How would you structure a front-end codebase that fifty engineers across several teams work on?
questions.zh: 一个由好几个团队、五十名工程师共同开发的前端代码库，你会怎么组织？
outline: Organize by feature or domain, not by file type
Enforce module boundaries with lint rules and public entry points
A shared design system and utilities, owned by a platform team
Monorepo with cached builds, code owners, and CI that tests only affected code
Agree on conventions for data fetching, state, errors, and testing
followUps: How do you keep build and CI times under control as the repo grows?

questions.prompt: What's your take on micro-frontends? When are they worth it?
questions.zh: 你怎么看微前端？什么时候才值得上？
outline: They solve an organizational problem: teams that must deploy independently
Costs: duplicated dependencies, inconsistent UX, harder shared state and routing
Runtime integration such as Module Federation versus build-time packages
Shared library versions become a coordination problem
For one team or a small app, a modular monolith is simpler

chunks.zh: 不值得为此增加复杂度

followUps: How would you share authentication and a design system across them?

questions.prompt: How have you used TypeScript to actually prevent bugs on a team, beyond just adding type annotations?
questions.zh: 除了加类型标注之外，你是怎么在团队里用 TypeScript 真正防住 bug 的？
outline: Turn on strict mode and treat any as a review smell
Model UI and domain states with discriminated unions; make invalid states unrepresentable
Generate API types from the schema instead of writing them by hand
Types vanish at runtime, so validate external data at the boundary
Keep types readable: clever generics hurt maintenance and compile time
followUps: Where do you draw the line between type safety and over-engineered types?

questions.prompt: How would you migrate a large JavaScript codebase to TypeScript without stopping feature work?
questions.zh: 在不停下功能开发的前提下，你会怎么把一个很大的 JavaScript 代码库迁到 TypeScript？
outline: Go incrementally: allow JavaScript and TypeScript side by side, convert file by file
Type the shared boundaries first: API layer, utilities, core models
Start loose, then tighten strictness flags one at a time
Block new JavaScript files in CI and track progress visibly
Explain the payoff to the team early to keep momentum
followUps: How do you deal with third-party libraries that have poor or missing types?

questions.prompt: If you were starting a new product today, how would you choose between React and Vue?
questions.zh: 如果今天要启动一个新产品，你会怎么在 React 和 Vue 之间做选择？
outline: Start from the team: existing skills and the hiring pool
Ecosystem: React offers more choices; Vue ships an official router and store
Mental model: explicit re-renders and JSX versus reactive state and templates
Platform needs: Next.js or Nuxt, server rendering, React Native
Either works; consistency and team fluency matter more than the framework

chunks.zh: （框架）有主见的、替你定好做法的

followUps: What would make you change your mind halfway through the project?

questions.prompt: How do you avoid request waterfalls and chains of loading spinners in a component-driven app?
questions.zh: 在组件驱动的应用里，你怎么避免请求瀑布和一连串的加载转圈？
outline: Waterfalls come from nested components fetching only after they render
Hoist fetching to the route level and start requests in parallel
Or fetch on the server and stream the slow parts
Prefetch on hover or route intent; cache and deduplicate requests
Place Suspense boundaries deliberately so spinners do not cascade
followUps: How do you decide what to block on and what to stream in later?

questions.prompt: When do useMemo, useCallback, and React.memo actually help, and when are they wasted effort?
questions.zh: useMemo、useCallback 和 React.memo 什么时候真的有用，什么时候是白费功夫？
outline: Memoization trades memory and comparison cost for skipped work
It pays off for expensive computations and for memoized children needing stable props
One unstable prop defeats React.memo for the whole component
Fix the structure first: move state down, pass children as props
Measure with the profiler; React Compiler now automates most of this
followUps: How do you find out which component is re-rendering and why?
